 Follow Marvel’s Avengers: Secret Wars Gamble Breaks Its Winning Formula for the Best Reason
 Dan Girolamo Mon, November 16, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday is still over a month away, but Marvel is already looking ahead to Avengers: Secret Wars in 2027. Secret Wars will continue Doomsday's story, but it could represent a departure from Marvel's successful blueprint.
 During an interview with Empire , Marvel's Kevin Feige teased how Secret Wars is a "whole other genre of story" compared to Doomsday. Feige further called it a "unique story" that will take risks and surprise people. Ultimately, Feige hopes Secret Wars will be something that people have never seen before .
 Feige's comments suggest Secret Wars is going to pivot away from Marvel's winning formula. It's a risk which makes perfect sense and should excite, not scare, fans.
 Secret Wars should lean into being different instead of recreating Endgame
 It's fair to say that Secret Wars is to Doomsday what Endgame was to Infinity War . Secret Wars and Endgame are the culmination of their respective Avengers movies. With Infinity War, Marvel laid out a fast-paced story, with the heroes racing to complete their mission. Infinity War memorably had one of the bleakest endings in Marvel history, when Thanos wiped out half of the universe's population with the snap of a finger.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Endgame started off as a somber film about grief and reconciliation, before transforming into a redemption story of epic proportions. The movie capped off a decade's worth of storytelling with an emotional but hopeful ending.
 Never say never, but it's highly unlikely Marvel can ever recreate the success of Endgame. The emotional beats and signature moments that will be hard to recapture. Iron Man's sacrifice and Captain America's ending are two iconic moments in the MCU that will likely never be replicated. If Secret Wars tries to outdo those two moments, it will likely fail.
 Secret Wars can serve as the culmination to the Multiverse Saga and serve as a bridge to the MCU's future. That's totally fine and expected. However, if Secret Wars starts with the heroes grieving the deaths from the previous movie before ending with a gigantic team-up, it's not doing itself any favors. Fans have seen that formula before in Endgame. The worst thing Avengers: Secret Wars could be is Endgame 2.0.
 As an MCU fan, Feige's comments are exciting. Marvel needs to take more risks creatively. Feige might be exaggerating when he talks about a different genre, but I do believe Secret Wars can subvert our expectations of what is possible in an Avengers movie. With Marvel entering a new phase after Secret Wars, why not use this Avengers movie to try new things? Unless Doomsday is a total flop, Secret Wars can afford to take some chances, knowing it will likely be another billion-dollar hit for Marvel.
 Advertisement Advertisement If Marvel starts taking bigger creative chances in Secret Wars, it's positioned for a brighter future.
